newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say they are 10 km from Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say they are 10 km from Kisangani.

text.p: Zairean rebels have advanced to within 10 km (six miles) of the northeastern city of Kisangani, rebel radio said on Tuesday.

The Voice of the People, broadcasting in the eastern border town of Goma, also said that the southeastern lake port of Moba, 750 km (470 miles) to the south in the copper and cobalt mining Shaba region, had been captured on Sunday.

The radio said the fall of Kisangani, the base for an ineffective mercenary-backed government counter offensive, was imminent and repeated a March 13 deadline for Zaire army soldiers to give up their arms.
"Most of the people have fled Kisangani while soldiers are stealing, raping and killing," the radio said.

Government and rebels have attached huge symbolic value to Kisangani. It is strategically placed on the Zaire river, which flows down to the capital Kinshasa. Witnesses say troops have already started stopping and checking all boats heading west.
The radio said that in the battle for the Lake Tanganyika port of Moba three fighters loyal to Burundian Hutu rebel Leonard Nyangoma had been captured fighting on the government side.

The Alliance of Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, led by veteran guerrilla Laurent Kabila, rules at least a sixth of the vast central African state since launching its rebellion in October with a force spearheaded by ethnic Tutsis.
